name: Gaussian Process Methods
explanation: Multifidelity models and kernel methods achieve several improvements. Exact forward recovery under a quadratic structure must be distinguished from general inverse-map performance: Paper 44 has one win, one tie and one loss.

name: Space-Filling Designs
explanation: Exact exchanges, structural preservation and broader searches account for the main improvements. Some methods also change the feasible class of the original construction. Paper 83 remains unfinished because its integer program exceeds the available license capacity.

name: Optimization Methods
explanation: Paper 95 has no comparable experiments; Paper 17 is unfinished because the baseline encounters empty feasible rho intervals. An improved acquisition objective does not automatically improve the final evaluation metric.

name: Optimal Designs
explanation: Ties dominate, and some designs already attain the corresponding theoretical bounds. Papers 20, 87 and 89 include noncomparable experiments. Numerical optimality diagnostics do not constitute rigorous global certificates.

name: Minimum Aberration and Related Criteria
explanation: Both construction improvements and computational acceleration produce wins; some design-quality criteria already attain their relevant bounds. Paper 64 primarily compares runtime, not an improved aberration value.

name: Active Learning and Sequential Design
explanation: Paper 29 awaits final review because of fidelity issues in the sequential policy and posterior approximation. Paper 58 has conflicting constraints on splitting small leaves. Local variance reduction does not directly imply better prediction, contour estimation or an entire adaptive policy.

name: Order-of-Addition Designs
explanation: Some complete constructions have exact certificates; guarantees in some applications apply only to the fitted surrogate. Theoretical optimality, empirical prediction and computational efficiency require separate interpretations.

name: Big-Data Subsampling
explanation: Sampling benefits depend on information retention and the risk objective. Paper 1 has no wins, one tie and two losses. Removing difficult observations may discard predictive information; general risk dominance is unproved.

name: Classical Experimental Designs
explanation: The results include exact constructions, projection optimization and runtime improvements from equivalent implementations. Better design quality and faster computation should be interpreted separately.

name: Screening Designs
explanation: Most experiments tie. Conditional thresholds and geometric coverage bounds provide guarantees within their stated scope, not universal dominance in screening power.
